code:
trips = spark.read.parquet("/data/nyc_taxi/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet")

long_trips = trips.filter(col("trip_distance") > 10)
long_trips.show(5)

# Identical:
long_trips = trips.where(col("trip_distance") > 10)
caption: The PySpark equivalent of Lesson 24's Pandas boolean indexing.

code:
trips.filter(col("trip_distance") > 10)   # correct

trips.filter("trip_distance" > 10)        # WRONG
# compares a Python string to an integer --
# no connection to the DataFrame at all
caption: col() is what builds a real Spark condition Spark can evaluate.

code:
trips.filter(
  (col("trip_distance") > 10) & (col("fare_amount") > 50)
).show(5)

# Use & and | -- NOT Python's and/or
caption: Column objects overload & and | for this — each condition needs its own parens.
